pages.text: Two branches of physics are about time itself: $(thing)Origin$(), how a universe begins, and $(thing)Finality$(), how it ends. Origin starts with $(thing)The Hot Big Bang$(): run the expansion backwards and everything was once hotter and denser than the core of a star.

The $(thing)Friedmann equation$() says how fast space expands: H² = 8πGρ/3 − kc²/a² + Λc²/3. Matter and radiation slow it, curvature bends it, and the vacuum energy Λ - dark energy - takes over in the end. Exactly flat space has the critical density, about five protons per cubic metre.

$(li)$(thing)Primordial Nucleosynthesis$(): for three minutes the universe fused hydrogen into helium. $(item)Primordial Nucleosynthesis Ash$() comes from quark-gluon plasma (or reheating plasma) in the $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(li)$(thing)Cosmic Inflation$() and $(thing)Reheating$(): see the next chapter.$(li)$(thing)Leptogenesis$(), $(thing)Vacuum Stability$(), $(thing)Creation from Nothing$() and $(thing)Conformal Cyclic Cosmology$() come after.
